label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
UmbiloSpanner here, Durban, I can see your messages. First off: CONGRATS on the wedding, man, that's the main thing. The bakkie is the second thing, we'll get to it.

Now, put the phone down for a second and listen, because Kobus is going to cost you more money than my shop. Kobus means well but that is 1970s Land Rover thinking. A 2019 D-Max is common rail, petrol in there will chew the high pressure pump and the injectors. Topping up with diesel does NOTHING, you just keep the petrol in the tank and you burn the pump.

Here is what you do TONIGHT:

1. DO NOT crank it again. Not once. Every time it turns, that pump is running on petrol with no lubrication in it. Take the key out of your pocket and put it in your fiancée's handbag. Let her hold it. She will not be as trigger-happy as you.
2. Do not drive it. Tow it. Not to the nearest petrol station, to a workshop. It needs the pump and injectors pulled and checked properly before anyone promises you anything.
3. It already ran, stalled and you cranked it 5 or 6 times, so damage is possible. If the pump and injectors are actually fine, we drain the tank, flush the lines, fit a new fuel filter and bleed it. That is normally R2 500 to R4 500. If the pump is gone, then Tash's R40 000 is real and we'll talk about how to make that less painful. I can't promise you the total tonight, I need my eyes on it first.

My shop is in Umbilo, open Saturday 7 till 12. Thabo, my guy, can drain that tank first thing tomorrow morning so it's not sitting there all night with petrol in it. Ring me tonight and I'll have him ready for you.

One more money tip: before you pay a tow truck cash, phone your insurance. Most policies include roadside assistance and towing. Check your policy first.

And Sizwe: borrow a bakkie for the cake and the sound system anyway. Do not plan your wedding around a drained tank. While you are at it, ask the groom's cousin with the R40 000 D-Max to borrow yours for the braai, he can start a fire with it and everyone will laugh.

Also, I will make you a sticker for the fuel flap, I promise you. We had a customer do this twice in the same year at the same garage and now he has a big yellow sticker on his flap that says PETROL. DIESEL. in three languages.

One last thing. In 1995, I was an apprentice. I put diesel in my boss's Golf. Nine years later he still tells that story at every braai. Your wedding is tomorrow, Sizwe, I am not going to be that guy at your braai in 20 years. Turn that engine off, call your insurance, and go home to your bride.

Calm down. It's a bakkie, not a divorce. We'll sort the D-Max.

UmbiloSpanner
